bill.name: Life Month Resolution (S.J. Res. 56)
bill.status: Introduced in Senate · Cruz · read twice and referred to Senate Judiciary on 2025-06-03

sourceLimits: The supplied 2,921-byte, 491-word raw source is a flattened extraction of the introduced-in-Senate version. It contains the seven recitals and both sections but has no page boundaries or metadata sidecar and omits the standard resolving formula visible in the matching official three-page PDF. Congress.gov metadata checked separately reports the measure as introduced, with the June 3, 2025 Judiciary referral as its latest action. Section 1 only supplies a short title. Section 2 makes a symbolic annual designation, records congressional recognitions and a commendation, and urges unspecified future policymaking; it does not amend law, appropriate or authorize funds, assign an implementing agency, create a program or benefit, require a report, set a quantitative target, state an express or delayed effective date, or establish a recurring data product. Although the long title identifies June, §2(1) itself says only “a Life Month” and supplies no first year, responsible actor, or annual renewal procedure. The resolution establishes no causal link to abortion incidence, births, pregnancy-resource-center activity, public opinion, future legislation, or resources for women and families. Legislative status is a one-time categorical event, not a recurring policy-outcome series, and a conditional on the resolution's own statements taking effect upon enactment would be tautological. Accordingly, this extraction has one substantive provision, four literal or expressive goals, three enactment-contingent expressive effects, and zero implementation barriers, forecastable metrics, stance matrices, series hints, or conditionals. No downstream outcome is inferred.

provisions.title: Section 2 — Life Month
provisions.heading: Annual Life Month designation, congressional statements, commendation, and policy exhortation
provisions.quote: That the Senate and the House of Representatives— (1) designate a Life Month annually; (2) recognize that every human life is a sacred gift from God, possessing inherent dignity and worth; (3) reaffirm the fundamental truth recognized in the Declaration of Independence that life is an unalienable right; (4) commend individuals, parents, families, faith-based organizations, and communities who work to promote a culture of life; and (5) urge policymakers to defend the sanctity of human life by enacting laws that protect the unborn and provide resources to empower women and families to choose life.
provisions.context: S.J. Res. 56 is an introduced ceremonial joint resolution. Its seven recitals present the resolution's right-to-life premises and praise organizations and families that support pregnant women and families; those recitals are stated rationales, not findings independently established by this source. Section 1 only gives the measure its short title. Section 2 contains five operative clauses: an annual designation, two statements of congressional belief, a commendation, and an exhortation to future policymakers. The official long title says the designated month is June, but §2(1) says only “a Life Month” annually and does not specify a first year, responsible actor, or renewal process. If enacted, the resolution would record those symbolic and expressive acts. It would not itself enact the laws or provide the resources urged in §2(5), and it creates no implementation machinery or measurable policy outcome.
goals: Designate an annual “Life Month,” with the resolution's long title identifying June even though §2(1) does not repeat the month.
Formally recognize the resolution's statement that every human life is a sacred gift possessing inherent dignity and worth, and reaffirm its statement that life is an unalienable right.
Commend the listed individuals, families, faith-based organizations, and communities that work to promote what the resolution calls a culture of life.
Urge policymakers to enact unspecified laws protecting the unborn and to provide unspecified resources intended to empower women and families to choose life.

effects.text: If enacted, the resolution would express Congress's designation of an annual Life Month; it supplies no first year, responsible actor, renewal process, or independently operative program.

If enacted, the resolution would record the recognitions, reaffirmation, and commendation in §2(2)–(4), but those statements do not themselves create enforceable rights, duties, eligibility rules, funding, or services.
Section 2(5) would urge unspecified policymakers to pursue future laws and resources; it neither enacts those laws nor appropriates, authorizes, or directs the provision of those resources.
